headline: Physics students to get full marks for two wrong questions in HSC
summary: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Million announced the decision in Parliament on Tuesday, amid ongoing student protests over exam conditions.
details: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Million announced in the National Parliament on Tuesday that students will receive full marks for two incorrect questions in the Physics paper of the ongoing HSC examinations.
The Minister stated that if errors occurred at any examination center, the authorities would conduct re-examinations if necessary.
The announcement comes amid widespread student protests in Dhaka and other parts of the country, including Chittagong, where students blocked gates to demand the Minister's resignation.
Addressing the decision to continue exams during severe weather, the Minister explained that the exams remained scheduled because officials had predicted the weather would be good.
Minister Million requested students to leave the streets and return to their studies, urging them to focus on their academic goals.
caption:
Full marks for wrong questions! The Education Minister has addressed the HSC Physics paper errors and student protests in Parliament.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Million announced in the National Parliament on Tuesday that students will receive full marks for two incorrect questions in the Physics paper of the ongoing HSC examinations.

The Minister stated that if errors occurred at any examination center, the authorities would conduct re-examinations if necessary.

The announcement comes amid widespread student protests in Dhaka and other parts of the country, including Chittagong, where students blocked gates to demand the Minister's resignation.

Addressing the decision to continue exams during severe weather, the Minister explained that the exams remained scheduled because officials had predicted the weather would be good.

Minister Million requested students to leave the streets and return to their studies, urging them to focus on their academic goals.

#HSC #Bangladesh #Education #StudentProtest #Physics

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, Somoy News

headline: 766 children dead from measles in Bangladesh
summary: Seven more children died within 24 hours as the measles death toll continues to rise.
details: The measles death toll in Bangladesh has reached 766, following the deaths of seven more children within a single 24-hour period.
The surge in cases is causing significant concern across the country as more children succumb to the virus and its complications.
Health authorities are monitoring the situation closely to manage the outbreak and prevent further loss of life.
Parents are urged to ensure their children are vaccinated to protect them from this preventable disease.
